clue.text: Awkward to do experiment involving radium

parts.note: to do someone is to con or swindle them

indicators.note: involving means the experiment word wraps round the radium symbol

parts.note: a try is an attempt or experiment
Ra is the chemical symbol for radium

explanation.surface: Doing an experiment that uses radium is a tricky business.
explanation.definitionFit: A contrary person is perverse and difficult, so awkward in temperament.

clue.text: "We're in row three" he advises monarch

parts.note: the third row of a theatre is row C, so three gives the letter C
we're in it, so it is ours: the possessive our
a tier is a row of seats

explanation.surface: A royal adviser announces where his party is seated in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the quotation as 'C is our tier': row three of seating is row C, and the speaker says that row is theirs.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtier attends at a royal court and counsels the sovereign.

clue.text: Tiny country pub's interior managed to retain posh lifts

indicators.note: lifts in a down clue means the piece is raised, so read upwards
to retain means the managed word holds the posh letter

parts.note: ran means managed, as a business
U means upper-class, posh

indicators.note: interior means the middle letter of the pub word

explanation.surface: A small nation's pub is run so as to keep the smart set coming upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retain' puts U inside RAN to give RUAN, which 'lifts' turns to NAUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru is a Pacific island republic, one of the smallest countries in the world.

clue.text: Stooped, as fat person ought to, before duke

parts.note: a fat person is round
should means ought to
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: An overweight person bows in front of a duke.
explanation.definitionFit: Being round-shouldered means having a stooping posture with forward-curved shoulders.

clue.text: Game daughter, clothing shed, looking embarrassed?

indicators.note: clothing means the game and daughter letters dress round the shed word

parts.note: RU is rugby union
a byre is a cowshed

explanation.surface: A sporty daughter, having shed her clothes, looks flushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a verb about undressing; it is the noun, a cowshed (BYRE).
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby red is a deep red, the colour of a blushing face.

clue.text: Relative to get Old King Cole making entrance

indicators.note: making an entrance means the singer's first name goes in among the other letters

parts.note: to get old is to age
Nat King Cole was the American singer, so King Cole gives his first name Nat

explanation.surface: A family member arrives in the guise of the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old King Cole' looks like the nursery-rhyme monarch, but 'Old' belongs with 'to get' (AGE) and 'King Cole' is the singer Nat King Cole.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnate is a kinsman descended through the male line, a type of relative.

clue.text: Don't hold adage to be self-evident

parts.note: to go without is not to have or hold something
a saying is an adage

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to accept an old proverb as obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that goes without saying is so obvious it needs no stating.

clue.text: Order starter and eat using last of pilau, unusually

indicators.note: unusually means the letters are arranged in an unusual way
last of means the final letter of pilau is taken

explanation.surface: A diner orders a starter and eats it with the end of a rice dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' gives U from pilau, and 'unusually' rearranges EATUSING plus U.
explanation.definitionFit: St Augustine is the saint whose rule founded the Augustinian religious order.

clue.text: Fellow's art deserving to be spoken of

indicators.note: to be spoken of means the archaic phrase is pronounced, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: thou earnest is the old second-person form, you art deserving

explanation.surface: A man's artwork merits being talked about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is not painting but the archaic 'thou art'; 'thou earnest' means you are deserving.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a man's first name, so a fellow in crossword terms.

clue.text: Nervous and upset, I retreat inside

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the assembled piece is turned upside down
inside means the retreat word sits within the self word

parts.note: the ego is the I, the self
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: Anxious and distressed, someone withdraws indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is the self, not the letter. 'upset' works because this is a down clue: the assembled letters are read from the bottom up, giving EGDENO turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: On edge is an idiom for tense and jumpy.

clue.text: Rock music blaring out from auditorium every second

indicators.note: every second means the second letter of each of the five words that follow is taken

explanation.surface: Loud rock music pours out of a concert hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock music' looks like a genre, but 'Rock' alone is the definition: Uluru, the great sandstone monolith in central Australia, once called Ayers Rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Uluru is the vast sandstone monolith in central Australia, formerly known as Ayers Rock.

clue.text: Can't stop shaking, following gang: I might be jumped on

indicators.note: following means the shaking phrase comes after the gang word

parts.note: a band is a gang or group of people
to wag on is to keep shaking, unable to stop

explanation.surface: A nervous recruit trembles uncontrollably after joining a gang.
explanation.definitionFit: Joining a popular cause is jumping on the bandwagon, so the wagon is what gets jumped on.

clue.text: Did like the Times revealing where its staff work on Thursday!

indicators.note: on means the staff phrase is placed onto Thursday, so it follows that abbreviation

parts.note: a newspaper's staff work under the editor, ED being the usual short form

explanation.surface: The newspaper boasts about its staff putting in their hours on a Thursday.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times was long nicknamed The Thunderer, so to behave like the Times is to have thundered.
explanation.definitionFit: The Times newspaper's old nickname is The Thunderer, so acting like it means roaring out opinions.

clue.text: Jobs of work with university for a feature on Morse

definitions.note: plural answer for a singular phrase: the pair of tusks is the walrus's feature taken as one

indicators.note: for means the university letter stands in place of the letter a

parts.note: tasks are jobs of work

explanation.surface: Office chores and a college course appear in an episode of the TV detective show.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse here is not the detective but the old word for a walrus, whose tusks are its most striking feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse is an archaic name for the walrus, whose long ivory teeth are its defining feature.

clue.text: Tree had pieces attached to the ground

indicators.note: in pieces signals that the letters of the tree phrase are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A fallen tree lies in fragments on the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' scrambles TREEHAD into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical device that is earthed is connected to the ground for safety.

clue.text: Permissive chap's got angry, apparently, on such important occasions

parts.note: someone who has got angry looks red in the face
a letter is one who lets, permits

explanation.surface: A lenient man flushes with fury on certain big days.
explanation.walkthrough: Important days were printed in red in old calendars, hence red-letter days.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-letter day is a memorable or significant one, so the adjective means important.

clue.text: Colourful, neat, cutting quote recalled

indicators.note: recalled means the whole assembled piece is called back, read in reverse
cutting means the cattle word slices into the quote word

parts.note: to quote a source is to cite it
neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox

explanation.surface: A tidy, incisive quotation is brought back to mind as vivid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' is the old word for cattle, not tidy. 'cutting' gives CITOXE and 'recalled' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotic things are strikingly unusual and bright, so colourful in a loose sense.

clue.text: Element supplying hotel with information

parts.note: a hydro is a spa hotel, originally one offering water cures
gen is slang for information

explanation.surface: A hotel supplies guests with details of the elements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hotel' would usually be H; here it is HYDRO, a spa hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrogen is the lightest chemical element.

clue.text: Bring small change to commercial fair

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
just means fair

explanation.surface: Someone brings coins to a trade fair.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust something is to make a slight alteration to it.

clue.text: Decapitate rat-like bats one shot with rabbit

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the remaining letters are jumbled
decapitate means the head, the first letter, is cut off

explanation.surface: A creature resembling a rat is beheaded and bats fly at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decapitate' leaves ATLIKE, which 'bats' rearranges. Rabbit is British slang for talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A talkie is a film with a soundtrack, one shot with talk (rabbit is slang for chatter).

clue.text: In passing round article get two copies of Times

indicators.note: round means the two copies go about the article
two copies of means the word for times is written twice

parts.note: by means times, as in five by three
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone buys two copies of the Times newspaper to get an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' in italics suggests the newspaper, but it is the multiplication sign read as BY.
explanation.definitionFit: By the by is an idiom for incidentally, said in passing.

clue.text: Sibling rivals playing tricks on royal surveyor

parts.note: bro is short for brother, a sibling
in bridge, a trick-taking game, West and South are opponents
ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Competing brothers and sisters play pranks on the king's surveyor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing tricks' sounds like mischief but refers to bridge, where W and S are on rival sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A browser surveys goods or pages casually, so is one who looks over things.

clue.text: Statesman put out a hand, having fended off extremists

indicators.note: with the outermost letters of the phrase kept off, what remains is the run inside it

explanation.surface: A politician holds out his hand after warding off radicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' is a link: put out a hand with its ends fended off. A statesman here is someone from a US state, Utah.
explanation.definitionFit: A Utahan is a native of the state of Utah, so a statesman in the punning sense.

clue.text: Flower on border needs pot after time

indicators.note: after means the cannabis word comes behind the time letter

parts.note: pot and weed are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A gardener's plant pot is overrun with weeds after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' in crosswords is a river; the Tweed forms part of the border between England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is a river that runs along part of the Anglo-Scottish border.

clue.text: Attractive person should keep to the back, mind

indicators.note: should keep means the attractive person holds the rearward word inside

parts.note: a looker is an attractive person
aft means towards the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Good-looking people are told to stay at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To look after something is to mind it or take care of it.

clue.text: Dunce gets mark denoting error in dividing

indicators.note: in means the error mark is placed inside the dunce word

parts.note: a twit is a fool or dunce
a cross, X, marks a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A dim pupil gets a cross for a mistake in long division.
explanation.definitionFit: Twixt is a poetic form of betwixt, meaning between, what lies dividing two things.

clue.text: Impact golden girl makes hard to predict

parts.note: a hit is an impact
or is the heraldic word for gold
a miss is a girl

explanation.surface: A golden girl's arrival has an unpredictable effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hit-or-miss is erratic, so its outcome cannot be forecast.

clue.text: Topcoat and one end of cardigan engulfed by smoke

parts.note: I is the roman numeral one

indicators.note: engulfed by means the end letter is swallowed by the smoke word

parts.note: a cig is a cigarette, a smoke

indicators.note: end of means only the final letter of cardigan is taken

explanation.surface: A coat and a cardigan are wreathed in smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topcoat' suggests an overcoat but here means the top layer on a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the sugar coating spread over the top of a cake.

clue.text: S. American poet, once around, has oddly to disappear

indicators.note: oddly to disappear means the odd-numbered letters of the phrase are dropped, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A Latin American poet who was once nearby has strangely vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the 1st, 3rd, 5th letters and so on across 'once around has' and the even letters remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Neruda was a Chilean poet and Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Following shot ring the alarm

parts.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or broken, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: After the gunshot, someone rings the alarm bell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges RINGTHE into RIGHTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To alarm someone is to scare them, a direct synonym.
